verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is from Kennedy Space Center on April 1, 2026, 6:24 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'no earlier than 6:24 p.m. EDT, Wednesday, April 1... at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R3: 'launch... on Wednesday, April 1, 2026... 6:24 p.m. ET... from Kennedy Space Center'; R4: 'April 1, at 6:24 p.m.... from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Pad 39B'; R5: '6:24 p.m. EDT Wednesday... from the Kennedy Space Center'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm location, date, year, and exact time.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is expected to be visible across most of Florida and parts of southern Georgia.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'visible across most of Florida and into parts of Georgia'; R4: 'Nearly all of Florida... and those in southern Georgia'; R5: 'across most of Florida and southeastern Georgia'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state visibility across most of Florida and southern/southeastern Georgia.

verifications.claim: Visibility maps show the rocket will be visible for roughly 10–70 seconds after liftoff for, respectively, the Space Coast and further inland.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: visibility map details from '+10 seconds, Space Coast' to '+70 seconds'; R4: 'first 70 seconds... Those furthest away... first 70 seconds'; R5: 'between about 10 seconds to 70 seconds after liftoff'
verifications.reasoning: Maps in sources specify 10s near Space Coast to 70s further inland.

verifications.claim: The rocket ascends to 40,000 feet before exiting direct visibility range.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Once the rocket reaches 40,000 feet, it will be out of the visibility range, NASA said'

verifications.claim: 10–20 seconds post-launch best viewed from Florida's Space Coast, Orlando area, Kissimmee, and north Treasure Coast.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: '1: Launch + 10 seconds, Space Coast, east Orlando'; '2: Launch + 20 seconds... Orlando... Kissimmee, the northern part of the Treasure Coast'
verifications.reasoning: Visibility map directly lists these areas for 10-20 seconds post-launch.

verifications.claim: 30–40 seconds post-launch visible throughout most of Central and North Florida, including Gainesville, Ocala, and Tampa.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: '+30 seconds... Ocala, Lakeland area, Central Florida'; '+40 seconds... Gainesville... Tampa'
verifications.reasoning: Map specifies these cities and regions for 30-40 seconds.

verifications.claim: 50–70 seconds post-launch potential visibility extends into southern Georgia, including Valdosta and near Brunswick, as well as northernmost Florida regions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: '+50 seconds... just outside Brunswick, Georgia, and Valdosta, Georgia'; '+60 seconds... Southern Georgia'; '+70 seconds... south past Miami to South Georgia'
verifications.reasoning: Map details exactly these areas and Georgia locations for 50-70 seconds.

verifications.claim: The launch is scheduled for early evening at 6:24 PM.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R3/R4/R5: all state '6:24 p.m.' (early evening time)
verifications.reasoning: Exact time confirmed; 6:24 p.m. is early evening.

verifications.claim: The launch at 6:24 PM will still be daylight.
verifications.label: OMITTED
